---
title: "Graduate Outcomes Summary (synthetic data)"
output:
  pdf_document:
    toc: false
params:
  data_path: "data/clean_survey.csv"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr); library(ggplot2)
source("R/data_functions.R")
d <- load_outcomes(params$data_path)
k <- kpis(d)
```

All figures come from a synthetic survey of `r format(k$respondents, big.mark = ",")` fictional graduates at 12 fictional institutions.

**Employed within 6 months (weighted):** `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * k$employment_rate)`. **Median hourly wage:** `r sprintf("$%.2f", k$median_wage)`.

## By program area

```{r t1}
t <- summarise_by(d, "program_area")
knitr::kable(transmute(t, `Program area` = program_area, n = n, `Employed (%)` = round(100 * employment_rate, 1), `Median wage ($)` = round(median_wage, 2)))
```

```{r p1, fig.height=3, fig.width=6}
ggplot(t, aes(reorder(program_area, employment_rate), employment_rate)) + geom_col(fill = "#2b6cb0") + coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Employed within 6 months") + theme_minimal()
```

## By institution

```{r t2}
ti <- summarise_by(d, "institution_id")
knitr::kable(transmute(ti, Institution = institution_id, n = n, `Employed (%)` = round(100 * employment_rate, 1), `Median wage ($)` = round(median_wage, 2)))
```
